experiment: HLS N×K joint assignment: SciPy linear-sum solver vs greedy and best fixed mapping

ontology.A_scenario: Three simultaneous task types and three agents; each edge has an explicit exogenous reward; one unit per match; constant competence and no learning.
ontology.B_mechanisms: No capability-transition mechanism is active; competence fields remain constant and rewards are exogenous assignment values.
ontology.C_organization: Joint per-period maximum-weight bipartite matching via SciPy linear_sum_assignment; compared with deterministic global-edge greedy and best episode-level fixed permutation.

configuration.reward_generation: Python random.Random(seed), independent uniform integer in [1,100] divided by 100 for each agent-task edge and period.
configuration.competence: constant placeholder 0.5; not used to generate rewards
configuration.resource_contract: same N×K geometry: individual limit 1, collective/problem budget 3; each selected edge consumes one resource; no agent/task may be used twice per period.
configuration.objective: maximize sum of selected edge rewards; assignments may remain unmatched if optional maximum-reward objective prefers it.
configuration.fixed_baseline: best of all 3! task-to-agent one-to-one mappings over the full 12-matrix episode; offline optimized within the declared fixed class. Its timing includes this per-episode map fit, not the subsequent lookup.
configuration.greedy_baseline: sort all current-period edges by descending reward, tie by agent then task index, accept if both endpoints remain unused and resource permits.
configuration.solver: scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment; SciPy modified Jonker–Volgenant backend solving the linear assignment objective, not a literal implementation of Kuhn's 1955 procedure.

BEST_FIXED.computation_timing_scope: episode-level offline permutation search over 3! maps

limitations: This validates a discrete unit-effort one-to-one matching restriction, not arbitrary fractional N×K allocations.
Rewards are synthetic, additive, fully observed, and exogenous; no CES complementarity, learning, transfer, uncertainty, or real task execution is represented.
The fixed baseline is optimized with full episode knowledge, while Hungarian and greedy react to each current matrix; this is deliberately a strong static reference.
SciPy's backend is an equivalent linear-sum assignment optimizer based on modified Jonker–Volgenant, not a code-level reproduction of Kuhn's Hungarian steps.
Timing is local diagnostic data and is not a hardware-independent performance claim.
